summary: Refined the 'stats_engine.py' telemetry pipeline by integrating Bayesian inference, Sparse Gaussian Processes, and Hidden Markov Models to distinguish system noise from performance degradation. Optimized computational efficiency through bottom-up tabulation of covariance matrices and implemented robust probabilistic state classification to ensure architectural reliability.
key_learnings: Sparse GP approximations (SVGP) and heteroscedastic modeling are essential for scalable, uncertainty-aware telemetry.
HMMs provide a robust framework for mapping continuous noise to discrete operational states, requiring log-space arithmetic for numerical stability.
Bottom-up tabulation improves cache locality and memory efficiency over recursive memoization in high-frequency data streams.
AST-based parsing and Pydantic validation maintain system determinism, while UMAP/t-SNE aid in monitoring thematic drift.
